_about: Facts about the candidate. The form fillers answer ONLY from this file and stop on any question it does not cover. Everything here is a fictional example: replace every value. Keys starting with _ are comments.

candidate._phone_national: LinkedIn's phone box takes the number without the country code.

education._about: Used for school and degree dropdowns. Values separated by | are tried in order.

work_authorization._about: Per country. right_to_work: you may work there today. needs_sponsorship: you need the employer to sponsor a visa. The screening closes 'we will not sponsor' ads only where needs_sponsorship is true, and the form fillers answer sponsorship questions from the job's country.

Sweden.describe: I have the right to work in Sweden and do not need sponsorship.

default.describe: I will need visa sponsorship to work in this country.

compensation._about: number goes into numeric salary boxes, text into free-text ones. Pick it per country; default covers the rest.

languages._about: Answers for language-level dropdowns. Values separated by | are tried in order.

voluntary_self_identification._about: Default is to decline. Replace with real answers only if you want them filled automatically.

automation._resume_name_check: A substring of the CV file name. The Easy Apply runner stops if LinkedIn's review page shows a different resume.
automation._common_skills: Skills you will answer the default years for, and say Yes to in yes/no experience questions.
automation._niche_topics: Yes/no experience questions on these topics stop the runner instead of answering Yes.
automation._extra_answers: Your own [question regex, answer] pairs. They are checked FIRST, so they win over every built-in rule. Keep answers you would give on any form; anything job-specific belongs in the job's own entry.
